_note: v3.4: official DPD taxonomy AND visual symptoms in each prompt, instead of visual symptoms alone (v3). v3.3 (taxonomy only) was better on seen pairs (9.8% vs 7.8%), top-5 HM (31.1% vs 30.0%) and ranking among the unseen pairs (56.6% vs 48.5%), but worse on unseen top-1 (6.7% vs 14.6%), so the two kinds of text help different things. Zero-shot ablation of ONE change against v3 (everything else identical; v3: HM 10.2% top-1 / 30.0% top-5). Zero-shot has no validation split (nothing is trained or tuned), so v3 vs this run on the same test images is the comparison; differences of a point or less are within what template wording alone can shift.
_result: Combining does not beat v3 on top-1, but gives the best top-5 of any zero-shot run. Harmonic mean 8.4% top-1 / 33.0% top-5 (v3 10.2% / 30.0%; v3.3 taxonomy only 8.0% / 31.1%); seen 9.5%, unseen 7.6%. It behaves like the taxonomy-only run with a little of v3's unseen benefit back (grape_black_rot 59% in v3, 13% in v3.3, 25% here): the taxonomic text, placed first, dominates the prompt embedding. Ranking among the 10 unseen pairs stays strong (55.5%, v3 48.5%), so what costs unseen top-1 is the seen/unseen balance, which zero-shot cannot correct. Interpretation for trained models: calibration (gamma) fixes exactly that balance, so the better ranking and top-5 of taxonomy + symptoms might pay off once trained; that needs a trained run (e.g. v13's recipe with these descriptions) to settle.

prompts._note: v3's templates; each description = official taxonomic description + '; ' + v3's visual symptom description.
templates: a close-up photo of a {crop} leaf showing {disease}: {description}.
a field photo of {crop} leaves with {disease}: {description}.
healthy_templates: a close-up photo of a healthy {crop} leaf: {description}.
a field photo of healthy {crop} leaves: {description}.

runtime._note: Runs on the CPU only to leave memory for the overnight training queue running at the same time (two GPU jobs crashed v10 before). Image embeddings come from the shared cache (computed on the GPU for v1-v3), text encoding is fp32 either way, so results match a GPU run up to float rounding.
